Let \(f(g)=(\operatorname{fix}(g)-1)^6\). Then \(A_{\sigma,\tau}=f(\sigma^{-1}\tau)\), so \(A\) is the matrix of convolution by the central function \(f\) on the regular representation of \(S_6\).

The permutation character of \(S_6\) on \(\{1,\dots,6\}\) is \(\operatorname{fix}(g)\). Hence
\[
\operatorname{fix}(g)-1=\chi_{(5,1)}(g),
\]
the character of the standard representation \(V=S^{(5,1)}\). Therefore
\[
f(g)=\chi_{V^{\otimes 6}}(g).
\]

For an irreducible \(S^\lambda\) of dimension \(d_\lambda\), the central convolution operator acts by the scalar
\[
\alpha_\lambda=\frac{1}{d_\lambda}\sum_{g\in S_6} f(g)\chi_\lambda(g)
=\frac{720}{d_\lambda}\,m_\lambda,
\]
where \(m_\lambda\) is the multiplicity of \(S^\lambda\) in \(V^{\otimes 6}\). In the regular representation, \(S^\lambda\) occurs \(d_\lambda\) times, so
\[
\det A=\prod_{\lambda\vdash 6}\alpha_\lambda^{d_\lambda^2}.
\]

To compute \(m_\lambda\), use
\[
S^\lambda\otimes V
=
\operatorname{Ind}_{S_5}^{S_6}\operatorname{Res}_{S_5}^{S_6}S^\lambda-S^\lambda.
\]
Thus one removes a corner box from \(\lambda\), adds a corner box back, and subtracts the original \(\lambda\). Iterating from \(S^{(6)}\), the multiplicities in \(V^{\otimes 6}\) are:

\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrrrrrr}
\lambda &(6)&(5,1)&(4,2)&(4,1,1)&(3,3)&(3,2,1)&(3,1,1,1)&(2,2,2)&(2,2,1,1)&(2,1,1,1,1)&(1^6)\\
\hline
m_\lambda&41&161&241&251&120&340&190&90&150&70&10
\end{array}
\]

The corresponding dimensions and eigenvalues are:

\[
\begin{array}{c|r|r|r}
\lambda&d_\lambda&m_\lambda&\alpha_\lambda=720m_\lambda/d_\lambda\\
\hline
(6)&1&41&29520\\
(5,1)&5&161&23184\\
(4,2)&9&241&19280\\
(4,1,1)&10&251&18072\\
(3,3)&5&120&17280\\
(3,2,1)&16&340&15300\\
(3,1,1,1)&10&190&13680\\
(2,2,2)&5&90&12960\\
(2,2,1,1)&9&150&12000\\
(2,1,1,1,1)&5&70&10080\\
(1^6)&1&10&7200
\end{array}
\]

Hence
\[
\det A
=
\prod_{\lambda\vdash 6}\alpha_\lambda^{d_\lambda^2}.
\]
Factoring the product gives
\[
\boxed{
2^{2475}3^{1272}5^{1014}7^{50}17^{256}19^{100}23^{25}41\,241^{81}251^{100}
}.
\]
